title: Tanzania Visa: Full Guide
excerpt: Everything you need to know about getting a Tanzania visa before your Kilimanjaro climb: cost, processing time, visa type, and a step-by-step application walkthrough.
seoTitle: Tanzania Visa Guide for Kilimanjaro Climbers

content.value: You have planned your Kilimanjaro climb, locked in the dates, and started getting ready. One of the first things to sort out, long before you pack your bag, is the visa. Most visitors to Tanzania, including citizens of the UK, the EU and the United States, need a visa, and the good news is that the entire process is done online from home and is relatively straightforward if you know what to do.

This guide covers everything you need to know: how much it costs, how long it takes, which visa to apply for, and when to submit. At the end you will find a walkthrough of the application process itself, step by step.
Do I need a visa for Tanzania?

Almost certainly. Visitors from most countries, including the UK, the EU, the US, Canada and Australia, require a visa to enter Tanzania, including the Kilimanjaro region. A few countries, mostly in Africa, are exempt, so check the official list for your passport. The visa is issued electronically (eVisa) through the official website of the Tanzanian Immigration Department, and the entire application is submitted and paid for online.

There is also the option of a Visa on Arrival at the airport, but we at HighAir strongly recommend applying online in advance. The reason is simple: arriving with an approved, printed visa saves you queuing after a long flight, and removes any uncertainty at the moment you can least afford it.
How much does a Tanzania visa cost?

For tourism and trekking, the relevant visa is an Ordinary Visa, a single-entry visa. For most nationalities, including UK and EU citizens, it costs 50 US dollars and is valid for a stay of up to 90 days. US citizens pay 100 US dollars for the same visa.

Other visa types exist, including a multiple-entry visa and a business visa, but for the vast majority of people coming to climb Kilimanjaro, the Ordinary Visa is the right choice. One useful point: a single Ordinary Visa allows you to visit both mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, so if you want to add a beach break after the climb, you do not need a separate visa.
How long does the visa take?
The official processing time is up to 14 days from the date of submission. In practice, a response sometimes arrives sooner, but you should not count on that.

The practical takeaway: apply early. We recommend submitting at least three to four weeks before your flight. Applying early leaves room to handle any delays or requests for additional documents, and removes unnecessary stress in the days before departure, days better spent preparing and packing.
What to prepare before you start
Before you sit down to fill in the application, have a few things ready so the process moves without interruption:

content.title: Documents required for the application
items: A valid passport with at least six months of validity beyond your entry date into Tanzania
A scan of your passport photo page (image file, maximum 300KB)
A passport-style portrait photo (image file, maximum 300KB)
A credit card for payment at the end of the process

content.value: File size limits matter. The official website will reject files that exceed the allowed size.
The application process: an overview
The application is submitted through the official website of the Tanzanian Immigration Department. The process is divided into stages.

Starting out: go to the official website, select a new application, and fill in basic details including your email address, passport number and country of issue. You will receive an Application ID. Keep it. It allows you to track your application status and is the key if you need to return to the form later.
Personal details: the form moves through several screens covering personal information, contact details and address, and passport information. Every detail must match your passport exactly.

Visit details: here you indicate that you are applying for an Ordinary Visa for tourism purposes, select Kilimanjaro International Airport as your point of entry and exit, and enter your arrival date and intended length of stay.

Accommodation details: the form asks for the address of your accommodation in Tanzania. HighAir clients receive the exact accommodation details from us to fill in this field, along with the full guide, so there is no guesswork involved.
Documents and payment: upload the files you prepared, confirm the declaration, and pay the fee. Your visa approval will be sent to your email within 14 days.

content.title: ✦ A tip from the field
content.value: Sometimes the payment button on the website does not respond correctly. If this happens there is no need to panic. There is an alternative way to complete the payment, and the full guide we send to clients explains exactly how.

In summary

Getting a Tanzania visa is a relatively straightforward online process: an Ordinary Visa for 50 US dollars for most nationalities (100 for US citizens), processing time of up to 14 days, and a handful of documents to prepare in advance. The most important rule is to apply early, at least three to four weeks before your flight.

Important note: the prices and procedures in this article are correct as of November 2026. Visa rules and fees can change and differ by nationality. Before submitting your application, confirm the latest details for your passport on the official website of the Tanzanian Immigration Department.
Frequently asked questions
How much does a Tanzania visa cost?

An Ordinary Visa (single entry) for tourism costs 50 US dollars for most nationalities, including UK and EU citizens, and is valid for a stay of up to 90 days. US passport holders pay 100 US dollars for the same visa.
How long does the Tanzania visa take?
The official processing time is up to 14 days from submission. We recommend applying at least three to four weeks before your flight.
Can I get a visa on arrival at the airport?
A Visa on Arrival is available, but applying online in advance is strongly recommended to avoid queuing after a long flight and to remove any uncertainty on arrival.
Which visa do I need for Kilimanjaro?
An Ordinary Visa, a single-entry tourist visa. It covers the vast majority of climbers and also allows you to visit Zanzibar on the same visa.
What documents do I need for the application?
A valid passport, a scan of the passport photo page, a passport-style portrait photo, a return flight ticket in PDF format, and a credit card for payment.
